source: the 48 correct items Phase 1e routed to L2
note: 1e §2.2 estimated ~17 different-verb / ~10 string artefacts / 4 article-quantifier / ~18 different grammar = 49; this exact recount sums to 48

items.answer: They watch the volcano from the grassy ridge.
items.reference: They watch a volcano from the grassy ridge.
items.reason: 'the volcano' for lock 'a volcano': determiner alternative, noun intact

items.answer: From the grassy ridge, they watch the volcano.
items.reference: They watch a volcano from the grassy ridge.
items.reason: 'the volcano' for lock 'a volcano', clause order moved

items.answer: They observe the volcano from the grassy ridge.
items.reference: They watch a volcano from the grassy ridge.
items.reason: 'the volcano' for lock 'a volcano' (verb synonym observe/watch)

items.answer: Oh sure, there are loads of ads on this square, exactly what we needed.
items.reference: Of course this square has many advertisements, exactly what we needed.
items.reason: 'loads of ads' for the quantifier lock 'many'

items.answer: The engineer asked him when he would return the race car to the garage.
items.reference: The engineer asked him when he was bringing the race car back into the garage.
items.reason: 'would return' for lock 'would bring': modal+base intact

items.answer: If he were holding the screwdriver, the shelf would already be lying on the ground.
items.reference: If he held the screwdriver, that shelf would be on the floor by now.
items.reason: 'were holding' for the past simple 'held' in the 2nd conditional

items.answer: If it were him holding the screwdriver, that shelf would already be on the ground.
items.reference: If he held the screwdriver, that shelf would be on the floor by now.
items.reason: 'were him holding' for the past simple 'held'

items.answer: She succeeded in staying totally still until the dragonfly settled down.
items.reference: She managed to stay completely still until the dragonfly settled.
items.reason: 'succeeded in staying' for 'managed to stay': gerund for infinitive

items.answer: If she had worn the beige jacket, this look would never have come about.
items.reference: If she had taken the beige jacket, this look would never have happened.
items.reason: 'had worn' for lock 'had taken': had+participle intact

items.answer: If she'd taken the beige jacket, this look would never have existed.
items.reference: If she had taken the beige jacket, this look would never have happened.
items.reason: "she'd taken" = 'she had taken'

items.answer: Never before have we seen such a quiet group at sunset.
items.reference: Never had we seen a group this quiet at sunset.
items.reason: vetoed by the mistake library (step=mistake), not by the lock; F1/F2 never see it

items.answer: They had the kitchen filmed while they were assembling that rainbow plate.
items.reference: They had the kitchen filmed while they built the rainbow plate.
items.reason: 'had the kitchen filmed' vs the gap lock 'had .. filmed'

items.answer: They had someone film the kitchen while they were arranging that rainbow plate.
items.reference: They had the kitchen filmed while they built the rainbow plate.
items.reason: active causative 'had someone film' for the passive 'had .. filmed'

items.answer: While they were assembling the rainbow plate, they had the kitchen filmed.
items.reference: They had the kitchen filmed while they built the rainbow plate.
items.reason: 'had the kitchen filmed' vs the gap lock, clause order moved

items.answer: It's said that she spent the whole winter training at altitude.
items.reference: She is said to have trained at altitude all winter.
items.reason: "It's said" = 'it is said'

items.answer: He asked how long she had had that swelling on her leg.
items.reference: He asked how long the swelling had been sitting on her foot.
items.reason: 'had had' for lock 'had been': had+participle intact

items.answer: He is able to find her before he arrives home.
items.reference: He can find her before she gets home.
items.reason: 'is able to find' for the modal 'can'

items.answer: The galaxy is moving slowly over their heads.
items.reference: The galaxy moves slowly above their heads.
items.reason: non-verb lexical lock: 'over' for the preposition 'above'

items.answer: The cup is hot, so you have to hold it carefully.
items.reference: The glass is hot, so you must hold it carefully.
items.reason: 'have to hold' for 'must'

items.answer: The cup is hot, so you need to hold it carefully.
items.reference: The glass is hot, so you must hold it carefully.
items.reason: 'need to hold' for 'must'

items.answer: She usually stays under the roof, but today she's dancing in the rain.
items.reference: She usually stays dry, but today she is dancing in the rain.
items.reason: "she's dancing" = 'she is dancing'

items.answer: He has finally stamped the document, so he can go home.
items.reference: He has stamped the document at last, so she can finally go home.
items.reason: 'has finally stamped' vs lock 'has stamped'

items.answer: He has finally put a stamp on the document, so he can go home.
items.reference: He has stamped the document at last, so she can finally go home.
items.reason: 'has put a stamp on' for 'has stamped' (adverb inside as well)

items.answer: While the waves rolled in, the black cat didn't move a single whisker.
items.reference: While the waves were rolling in, the black cat did not move a whisker.
items.reason: past simple 'rolled' for the past continuous 'were rolling'

items.answer: The director said that they would shoot the office scene before lunch.
items.reference: The director said they would film the office scene before lunch.
items.reason: 'would shoot' for 'would film'

items.answer: The director said that they were going to shoot the office scene before lunch.
items.reference: The director said they would film the office scene before lunch.
items.reason: 'were going to shoot' for 'would film'

items.answer: The counter he is standing behind is older than the whole school.
items.reference: The podium that she is standing behind is older than the school.
items.reason: zero relative clause for the lock that/which/behind which

items.answer: The counter he stands behind is older than the entire school.
items.reference: The podium that she is standing behind is older than the school.
items.reason: zero relative clause for the lock that/which/behind which

items.answer: Her speech got rewritten twice before she had even walked onto that stage.
items.reference: Her speech was rewritten twice before she ever walked onto that stage.
items.reason: get-passive 'got rewritten' for the be-passive 'was rewritten'

items.answer: The frightening light has completely gone out and the station is dark once more.
items.reference: The eerie light has faded completely, and the yard is dark again.
items.reason: 'has completely gone out' vs lock 'has gone out'

items.answer: How long has he been holding that card up to the wrong door?
items.reference: How long has she been tapping that keycard on the wrong door?
items.reason: 'has he been holding' for 'has she been tapping' (pronoun differs too)

items.answer: How long has she been holding that card up to the wrong door?
items.reference: How long has she been tapping that keycard on the wrong door?
items.reason: 'has she been holding' for 'has she been tapping'

items.answer: How long has he been tapping that card on the wrong door?
items.reference: How long has she been tapping that keycard on the wrong door?
items.reason: 'has he been tapping': pronoun inside the locked span

items.answer: If he turns the ring once more, he will lower the price again.
items.reference: If he turns the ring once more, she will drop the price again.
items.reason: 'will lower' for lock 'will drop'

items.answer: If she turns the ring one more time, she'll lower the price again.
items.reference: If he turns the ring once more, she will drop the price again.
items.reason: "she'll lower": contraction plus a different verb

items.answer: If he turns the ring again, he will reduce the price once more.
items.reference: If he turns the ring once more, she will drop the price again.
items.reason: 'will reduce' for lock 'will drop'

items.answer: If the ball had fallen on black, she would have gone home empty-handed.
items.reference: If the ball had landed in black, she would have gone home with empty pockets.
items.reason: 'had fallen' for lock 'had landed'

items.answer: The security guard is sorry - he wishes he'd turned the camera toward the horizon a minute sooner.
items.reference: The guard wishes he had turned the camera towards the horizon a minute earlier.
items.reason: "he'd turned" = 'he had turned'

items.answer: He ought to have gone to the doctor a few days ago, but he waited until he could barely stand up.
items.reference: He should have seen a doctor days ago, but he waited until he could hardly stand.
items.reason: 'ought to have gone' for 'should have seen/gone'

items.answer: By Friday he will have reserved the fifth appointment at the studio.
items.reference: By Friday she will have booked a fifth appointment at the studio.
items.reason: 'will have reserved' for 'will have booked'

items.answer: At the moment he is pushing a blue compress against the bump.
items.reference: Right now he is holding a blue ice pack against the lump.
items.reason: 'is pushing' for 'is holding/is pressing'

items.answer: By ten o'clock, he will have been heating the noodles for two hours straight.
items.reference: By ten he will have been reheating noodles for two hours straight.
items.reason: 'will have been heating' for 'will have been reheating'

items.answer: By ten, she will have been warming up the noodles for two hours in a row.
items.reference: By ten he will have been reheating noodles for two hours straight.
items.reason: 'will have been warming up' for 'will have been reheating'

items.answer: The veranda that she now spends every morning on faces the sunrise.
items.reference: The veranda, where she now spends every morning, faces the sunrise.
items.reason: 'that she now spends every morning on': stranded preposition for where/on which

items.answer: The terminal was empty; nevertheless, she felt as if somebody was watching her.
items.reference: The terminal was empty; even so, she felt watched.
items.reason: non-verb lexical lock: 'nevertheless' for the linker 'even so'

items.answer: Although the terminal was empty, she had the feeling that someone was watching her.
items.reference: The terminal was empty; even so, she felt watched.
items.reason: 'Although the terminal was empty' instead of the practised linker

items.answer: Had he set off earlier, he would have missed the fog.
items.reference: If he had started earlier, he would have missed the mist.
items.reason: 'Had he set off': inversion puts a pronoun inside the span

items.answer: He would have missed the fog if he had set out earlier.
items.reference: If he had started earlier, he would have missed the mist.
items.reason: 'had set out' for 'had set off / had started / had left'
